title: Annual Cases of Abuse and Assaults against Bus Captains
what_it_is: Annual Cases of Abuse and Assaults against Bus Captains

sections.label: Bus captain abuse cases and penalties
sections.summary: The Government, PTOs and NTWU oppose abuse of bus captains; reported cases fell from 52 in 2019 to 27 in 2022, with prosecution possible and protective barriers discontinued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have shared previously in this House that the Government, our public transport operators, or PTOs, and the National Transport Workers’ Union, or NTWU, take a united and firm position against physical and verbal abuse of bus captains by a small minority of errant commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: There were 26 bus captain abuse cases by passengers reported by our PTOs in 2018, 52 in 2019, 50 in 2020, 35 in 2021, and 27 in 2022 thus far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Perpetrators may be prosecuted for offences under the Protection from Harassment Act and be liable on conviction for an imprisonment term of up to 12 months, a fine of up to $5,000, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They could also be charged for voluntarily causing hurt under the Penal Code, which carries an imprisonment term of up to three years, a fine of up to $5,000, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The installation of protective barriers in buses was trialled in 2018 and again in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: However, these were discontinued as bus captains had provided feedback that the glare from the barriers posed a safety risk when driving.

sections.label: Zero tolerance for abusive behaviour
sections.summary: The tripartite position has zero tolerance for abusive behaviour towards public transport workers, and existing measures may be reviewed if inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As I have said, our policy position – and this is not just that of the Government but also that of the PTOs and the unions – the tripartite position is clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have zero tolerance for such abusive behaviours towards our public transport workers and if the existing measures are not adequate, we are prepared to look at reviewing them.
